The stock did not suddenly move because of one announcement.

✅ Q4 FY26 turnaround → Market notices 🤞

Revenue +42% YoY
PAT turned positive
Base business grew ~36%
Base EBITDA margin reached ~26%

↓

Base business proves its quality → Market changes its view

Solara’s base API business is generating ~23–25% EBITDA margins.

But ibuprofen is very different:

₹100 base-business revenue → ~₹24 EBITDA

₹100 ibuprofen revenue → ~₹12 EBITDA loss

So investors started seeing two businesses inside Solara:

Base API business = Good, high-margin earnings engine

Ibuprofen = Structural drag

↓

Why is the base business special?

👉🏻 75%+ of the base business comes from regulated markets.

These markets have strict quality and regulatory requirements. Customers also take time to qualify suppliers, creating barriers to entry and making relationships stickier.

👉🏻 Solara has a differentiated niche in specialised polymer APIs.

These are more complex products and are not simply commodity chemicals. Solara has a strong position in certain polymer markets, giving it a degree of competitive advantage.

👉🏻 The business is diversified across 60+ APIs.

This reduces dependence on one single molecule and gives the company multiple avenues for growth.

👉🏻 Existing manufacturing capacity is only around ~70% utilised.

This means Solara can potentially grow revenue by increasing utilisation and improving product mix before making massive fresh capex.

👉🏻 New DMFs create a future product pipeline.

Management is targeting roughly 4–5 new DMF filings per year. These can become commercial products over the next 2–3 years.

👉🏻 CRAMS provides another long-term option.

It is still small today, but if it scales, it could add a higher-value, higher-margin business.

↓

Ibuprofen strategic review → Potential removal of the structural drag

Management appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options for ibuprofen.

Possible outcome:

Sale / restructuring / repurposing

The important point:

Solara does not necessarily need ibuprofen to become profitable.

Simply removing the loss-making business could improve overall earnings and capital efficiency.

FedFina: AUM Rs 21,136 cr (+35%), gold AUM Rs 11,191 cr (+77%), PAT Rs 114 cr (+53%)
CSB Bank: net advances Rs 40,309 cr (+24%), gold loans Rs 21,906 cr (+47%), PAT Rs 150 cr (+27%)

WHERE THE GROWTH CAME FROM

FedFina's CFO put a number on the swing: domestic gold prices fell roughly 15% between 31 January and 30 June. AUM growth this quarter had to come from tonnage and LTV, not price. Manappuram's tonnage rose 7% sequentially to 67 tonnes. FedFina's rose 1%, and its LTV on AUM moved from 61% to 68% because the collateral repriced down. Similar headline percentages to last year, different engine underneath.

YIELDS ARE THE REAL STORY

Muthoot's gold loan yield came in at 17.93%, against 19.56% in Q4 FY26 and 20.76% the quarter before. Management called last year's level a windfall from recoveries and renewals, and now guides 18% to 18.5%. Manappuram went the other way, up around 60 bps to 17.7% on corrective pricing, guiding to the same zone. Two of the largest players converging on one yield while both plan hundreds of new branches is what competition looks like before it reaches the P&L.

READ MUTHOOT STANDALONE

Consolidated PAT grew 43%. Standalone grew 25%. The gap is subsidiaries: Belstar swung from a loss to Rs 66 cr, Muthoot Money's PAT rose 366%. Consolidated PAT was also down 17% sequentially. The gold business is compounding, just not at 43%.

THE NEW RBI RULES

From 1 April, LTV on bullet loans is computed on principal plus interest at maturity. Lenders shifted to periodic interest structures, so a single missed interest payment now flags the whole loan overdue. FedFina's Stage 2 moved from 2.2% to 2.7% on this alone, and Muthoot said the same of its Stage 1 and 2. Both managements call it optical. Fair for now, and worth checking again in two quarters rather than taking on trust.

ONE MORE

IIFL's gold book at Rs 58,406 cr is now larger than Manappuram's Rs 57,006 cr. Though roughly 35% of IIFL's total AUM sits off balance sheet, through co-lending and assignment together, so scale and capital at risk are not the same number.

THE CATCH

Muthoot guides 15% AUM growth for FY27 after delivering 49% in FY26, and declined to guide on profit. Manappuram and FedFina both guide 25% to 30% on gold. The largest lender in the sector and its two challengers are describing the same product in the same year very differently. CSB called Q1 its worst NIM quarter of the year at 3.66%. The FY26 earnings base is being described by the people who produced it as not repeatable.

FY26 was a price story, and AUM growth was the right single metric. FY27 needs tonnage, yield and credit cost sitting next to it.
